description: B2's package -> algorithm table. If this package is in the dependency graph, which quantum-relevant primitives does it put there? Moved out of lib/collectors/src/crypto-packages.ts on 2026-08-14 so a data revision needs no code edit (C1's rule) and so check:standards polices its retrievedAt dates (G-14).
criticalCaveat: A lockfile records the fully RESOLVED dependency graph. A package matched here may be a transitive dependency of the build toolchain rather than a library the project's own code calls. This table states what a package implements, never that the customer's code uses it — see the toolchainUbiquity flag and docs/Claude/09-open-gaps.md G-20.
curationRules: The algorithm must be a property of the package, not of how a caller configures it. JWT/JOSE libraries (jsonwebtoken, jose, pyjwt) are deliberately absent: their algorithm is an `alg` value chosen at runtime, so a lockfile entry says nothing about which one is in use. Inferring RSA from jsonwebtoken would manufacture findings, and a wrong value is worse than no value (G-05).
`algorithm` must be a canonicalName in algorithms.json, so algorithm-mapping.ts resolves severity/replacement/standard for it at read time. Asserted in algorithm-mapping.test.ts.

No version-range reasoning. The version a lockfile pins is recorded, but this table has no notion of `implemented from x.y.z` or `vulnerable before x.y.z`. Where a claim is known to be version-dependent it is marked needs-check rather than silently applied to every version — see paramiko/DSA below and G-21.

Every claim carries a citation with a verbatim quote from the package's own documentation. A citation without a quote is the unverified claim G-07/G-08/G-09 punished. Where no such quote could be obtained the claim is `needs-check`, not deleted: the gap being visible is the point.

statusValues.verified: A verbatim quote from the package's own documentation supports the claim, read on `retrievedAt`. It does NOT mean the claim was checked against the specific version a lockfile pins.
statusValues.needs-check: No supporting quote was obtained, or the source contradicts the claim for some versions. Carries no `retrievedAt`, because there is no re-verification date to age out — dating an unverified claim is exactly the failure check:standards cannot see.

dedicated.meaning: The package exists to implement this primitive. Presence implies the primitive is available and almost certainly used.
dedicated.rationale: A lockfile match is two claims of very different strength. That the package is in the dependency graph is near-certain: a lockfile is machine-generated and exactly parsed, with no equivalent of the regex collector's false positives on prose or comments — which is why this tier sits above the regex collector's 0.7. That the algorithm is therefore used follows almost automatically for a single-purpose library: nobody installs node-rsa for anything else.

multi-primitive.meaning: One of several primitives the package offers. Presence proves the library is shipped; which primitive the caller invokes is not visible in a lockfile.
multi-primitive.rationale: For a general-purpose library (cryptography, elliptic, node-forge) the second claim genuinely does not follow — the primitive is available, and which of several the caller actually invokes cannot be read from a lockfile. Neither tier approaches 1.0, which is reserved for evidence that observes the algorithm in operation (a completed TLS handshake), and neither is 0: static presence of a crypto library is real inventory evidence.

packages.name: node-rsa

citation.quote: RSA library for Node.js and browsers.

algorithms.rationale: node-rsa is an RSA implementation; its feature list is key generation, encryption/decryption and signing/verifying, and it offers no other public-key primitive.

packages.note: Bundles MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2 internally for padding and signature schemes. Those are not reported: an internal padding hash is not an algorithm choice the customer made.

citation.quote: Generate a RSA PEM key pair from pure JS

algorithms.rationale: keypair generates RSA key pairs and nothing else.

packages.name: node-forge

citation.quote: Provides [X.509][] certificate support, ED25519 key generation and signing/verifying, and RSA public and private key encoding, decoding, encryption/decryption, and signing/verifying.

algorithms.rationale: forge.pki implements RSA key generation, signing and encryption.
forge.pki.ed25519 implements Ed25519 signatures.

packages.note: The absence of ECDSA/ECDH is a checked absence, not an omission: the strings ecdsa, ecdh and elliptic do not occur anywhere in the README.

citation.quote: supporting RSA/RSAPSS/ECDSA/DSA signing/validation

algorithms.rationale: jsrsasign implements RSA and RSA-PSS signature. RSA *encryption* was removed in v11.0.0 (CVE-2024-21484, Marvin attack) — the README states PKCS#1.5 and RSAOAEP encryption/decryption are no longer supported — so the claim rests on signature alone.

jsrsasign implements ECDSA. Its curve set is not NIST-only: the ECDSA API page lists secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1 alongside the Koblitz curves secp256k1 and secp192k1, so no single curve is claimed here.
jsrsasign implements DSA signature.

citation.document: elliptic README (indutny/elliptic), ECDSA / EdDSA / ECDH sections and curve list
citation.quote: NOTE: That `curve25519` could not be used for ECDSA, use `ed25519` instead.

algorithms.rationale: elliptic implements ECDSA over secp256k1 and p192/p224/p256/p384/p521; curve-agnostic, so no key size is claimed.
elliptic's EdDSA implementation is instantiated as new EdDSA('ed25519') — ed25519 is the only EdDSA curve in its curve list.
elliptic implements ECDH key agreement (key.derive(otherPublic)).

packages.name: secp256k1

citation.quote: This module provides native bindings to bitcoin-core/secp256k1. In browser elliptic will be used as fallback.

algorithms.rationale: Bindings to libsecp256k1. ECDSA sign/verify/recover over secp256k1 is the package's primary purpose and it supports no other curve.
API.md documents an `ecdh` function — ECDH key agreement over secp256k1. Added 2026-08-14: the original hand-curated entry claimed ECDSA only.

packages.note: Browser builds fall back to the pure-JS `elliptic` package by the module's own README, so a project depending on this may also carry elliptic's claims transitively.

packages.name: @noble/secp256k1

citation.quote: Fastest 5KB JS implementation of secp256k1 signatures & ECDH.

algorithms.rationale: Single-curve ECDSA implementation (secp256k1), RFC6979-compliant.
getSharedSecret performs ECDH over secp256k1. Added 2026-08-14: the original hand-curated entry claimed ECDSA only.

packages.note: Also ships BIP340 Schnorr signatures. Not reported: Schnorr has no canonicalName in algorithms.json, and inventing one here would put an algorithm name in a place that cannot resolve a standard or a deadline for it.

packages.name: @noble/ed25519

citation.quote: Fastest 5KB JS implementation of ed25519 signatures.

algorithms.rationale: Single-curve Ed25519 signature implementation, RFC8032/FIPS 186-5.

packages.note: Deliberately excludes x25519/curve25519 since v2 — the README directs users needing key agreement to @noble/curves — so no ECDH/DH claim is made.

citation.quote: We provide ECDH over all Weierstrass curves, and over 2 Montgomery curves X25519 (Curve25519) & X448 (Curve448), conforming to [RFC 7748]

algorithms.rationale: Ships ECDSA over the NIST (p256/p384/p521), secp256k1 and Brainpool curves.
Ships ed25519 and ed448; curve-agnostic at the package level, so no key size is claimed.
Ships ECDH over all Weierstrass curves plus X25519 and X448.

citation.document: tweetnacl-js README (dchest/tweetnacl-js), Signatures and box sections
citation.quote: Implements *x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305*.

algorithms.rationale: nacl.sign implements ed25519 (README: 'Implements [ed25519]').
nacl.box is x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305; the raw X25519 primitive is nacl.scalarMult.

citation.quote: A native implementation of Ed25519 for Node.js.

algorithms.rationale: Native Ed25519 signature bindings (MakeKeypair/Sign/Verify).

packages.name: sshpk

citation.quote: Supports RSA, DSA, ECDSA (nistp-*) and ED25519 key types, in PEM (PKCS#1, PKCS#8) and OpenSSH formats.

algorithms.rationale: sshpk parses and generates SSH RSA keys.
sshpk supports SSH DSA keys.
sshpk supports ECDSA keys over nistp256/nistp384/nistp521; curve-agnostic at the package level.
sshpk supports ED25519 keys.

packages.note: Key *generation* is narrower than parsing — the README limits generation to ecdsa and ed25519 — but a dependency on the library still puts all four key types in reach.

citation.quote: Only secp256k1 curve, only SHA-512 (KDF), HMAC-SHA-256 (HMAC) and AES-256-CBC for ECIES

algorithms.rationale: eccrypto signs with ECDSA over secp256k1.
eccrypto derives shared secrets with ECDH over secp256k1.

citation.quote: a JavaScript function for hashing messages with MD5.

algorithms.rationale: The package is an MD5 implementation.

citation.quote: A simple and fast MD5 hash function for JavaScript supports UTF-8 encoding.

algorithms.rationale: The package is an MD5 implementation; it also exposes HMAC-MD5.

citation.quote: A simple SHA1 hash function for JavaScript supports UTF-8 encoding.

algorithms.rationale: The package is a SHA-1 implementation; it also exposes HMAC-SHA1.

citation.quote: SHA-1 -- **legacy, do not use in new systems**

algorithms.rationale: sha.js implements SHA-0, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 — SHA-1 included, and marked legacy by upstream itself. It does not implement SHA-3.

packages.name: crypto-js

citation.quote: - ```crypto-js/md5```

algorithms.rationale: CryptoJS.MD5 (crypto-js/md5) is part of the bundle, alongside HMAC-MD5.
CryptoJS.SHA1 (crypto-js/sha1) is part of the bundle, alongside HMAC-SHA1.

packages.note: The README states the project is no longer actively maintained and recommends the native Crypto API.

packages.name: cryptography

citation.quote: The ECDSA signature algorithm first standardized in NIST publication FIPS 186-3

algorithms.rationale: Implements RSA key generation, signing and encryption.
Implements ECDSA over the SECG/NIST curves (secp256r1 is documented as 'Also called NIST P-256').
Implements Ed25519 and Ed448 as separate modules; curve-agnostic at the package level, so no key size is claimed.
Implements ECDH (SP 800-56A) and finite-field Diffie-Hellman.

packages.note: The library's own DH page states that finite-field DH is deprecated and support will be removed in a future release. The ECDH half is unaffected.

citation.quote: DSA and ECDSA are U.S. federal standards for digital signatures, specified in FIPS PUB 186-4.

algorithms.rationale: Crypto.PublicKey.RSA defines RSA keys, private or public.
Crypto.PublicKey.DSA generates and constructs DSA keys; the DSS page calls plain DSA deprecated.
Crypto.Signature.DSS over Crypto.PublicKey.ECC is ECDSA. Its documentation restricts accepted ECC keys to P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521, so no single curve is claimed.

packages.name: pycryptodomex
packages.needsCheckReason: The claims below are transposed from pycryptodome, which shares the codebase under the `Cryptodome` namespace rather than `Crypto`. The Cryptodomex distribution's own documentation was not read separately, so this is an inference, not a citation.

citation.document: PyCryptodome documentation (the shared codebase; the Cryptodomex namespace was NOT separately verified)

algorithms.rationale: Cryptodome.PublicKey.RSA is expected to mirror pycryptodome's Crypto.PublicKey.RSA.
Cryptodome.PublicKey.DSA is expected to mirror pycryptodome's Crypto.PublicKey.DSA.
Cryptodome.Signature.DSS over ECC keys is expected to mirror pycryptodome's.

packages.name: pycrypto
packages.needsCheckReason: PyCrypto has been unmaintained since 2014 and no authoritative documentation for it was read. The claims below are the original hand-curated ones, retained rather than deleted so the gap stays visible.

algorithms.rationale: Crypto.PublicKey.RSA is believed to be part of PyCrypto (unmaintained).
Crypto.PublicKey.DSA is believed to be part of PyCrypto (unmaintained).

citation.quote: Representation of an ECDSA key which can be used to sign and verify SSH2 data.

algorithms.rationale: paramiko supports ssh-rsa and rsa-sha2-256/512 host and user keys.

algorithms.needsCheckReason: Version-dependent, and this table does no version-range reasoning (G-21). Paramiko's changelog for 4.0.0 (2025-08-03) states: 'Removed support for the DSA (aka DSS) key algorithm, as it has been badly outdated and insecure for a decade or more at this point, and was recently completely removed from OpenSSH as well.' DSSKey is absent from the current API docs. The claim holds for 3.x and is false for 4.x; the pinned version is recorded in the observation's evidence, so a reviewer can settle it.
algorithms.rationale: paramiko 3.x supports ssh-dss keys; 4.0.0 removed them.
paramiko supports ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521 keys via ECDSAKey.
paramiko supports ssh-ed25519 keys via Ed25519Key.

citation.quote: It supports encryption and decryption, signing and verifying signatures, and key generation according to PKCS#1 version 1.5.

algorithms.rationale: python-rsa is a pure-Python RSA implementation. Its own description scopes it to RSA and names no other algorithm.

citation.quote: This is an easy-to-use implementation of ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography) with support for ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm), EdDSA (Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm) and ECDH (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman), implemented purely in Python, released under the MIT license.

algorithms.rationale: Corrected 2026-08-14. The original entry rated this `dedicated` on the reasoning that 'python-ecdsa exists to implement ECDSA'. Its own description contradicts that: the package is a general ECC library offering ECDSA, EdDSA and ECDH, so which primitive a caller invokes is not readable from a lockfile. Curve-agnostic — NIST 192/224/256/384/521, Brainpool 160-512 and secp256k1 — so no key size is claimed.
Added 2026-08-14. Key generation, signing and verifying are supported for Ed25519 and Ed448; curve-agnostic between the two, so no key size is claimed.
Added 2026-08-14. Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman is named in the package's own description.

packages.name: ed25519

citation.quote: Python bindings to the Ed25519 public-key signature system.

algorithms.rationale: The package is an Ed25519 signature implementation.

packages.note: The README carries the header 'Not Recommended For New Applications: Use pynacl Instead'.

citation.document: PyNaCl documentation, signing and public-key encryption
citation.quote: Private key for producing digital signatures using the Ed25519 algorithm.

algorithms.rationale: nacl.signing is Ed25519; the docs note Ed25519 keys are 256 bits (32 bytes), which matches the curve bit size this table resolves.

nacl.public performs key agreement over Curve25519 (shared_key returns 'the Curve25519 shared secret'). The docs name the curve Curve25519 rather than X25519; these are the same 255-bit curve and the same 32-byte keys, so the key size is unaffected.

packages.name: pyopenssl

citation.quote: A class representing an DSA or RSA public key or key pair.

algorithms.rationale: PKey exposes OpenSSL RSA keys (OpenSSL.crypto.TYPE_RSA).
PKey exposes OpenSSL DSA keys (OpenSSL.crypto.TYPE_DSA).

packages.note: The ECDSA claim was REMOVED on 2026-08-14 as contradicted by the source. pyOpenSSL's PKey documents only TYPE_RSA and TYPE_DSA; there is no TYPE_EC. Its only EC surface is get_elliptic_curves(), whose documented purpose is choosing the curve for TLS ECDHE key exchange — not an EC key object and not ECDSA. Reporting ECDSA from a pyOpenSSL dependency would have been a customer-facing claim of the same class as G-07/G-08/G-09. The module is also documented as pending deprecation in favour of pyca/cryptography.

citation.quote: M2Crypto wrapper for OpenSSL ECDH/ECDSA API.

algorithms.rationale: M2Crypto wraps OpenSSL RSA.
M2Crypto wraps OpenSSL DSA.
M2Crypto.EC signs and verifies with ECDSA (methods are named sign_dsa/verify_dsa but documented as ECDSA).
M2Crypto wraps the OpenSSL DH API, and M2Crypto.EC.compute_dh_key performs ECDH.
